title: Agent Satisfaction Ranking
statement:
Track integer customer-satisfaction ratings for support agents and return qualified agents ranked from highest to lowest satisfaction.

Contract
- Construct an empty tracker with `new Solution()`.
- `recordScore(agentId, score)` records one integer rating for `agentId`. `agentId` must be non-null and non-blank, and `score` must be between `1` and `5` inclusive; otherwise throw `IllegalArgumentException`.
- `qualifiedAgents(minRatings)` (`minRatings >= 1`, otherwise throw `IllegalArgumentException`) returns a new list of every agent with at least `minRatings` recorded scores.
- Order qualified agents by highest exact average score first, then by higher total rating count, and finally alphabetically (`String.compareTo`) when both average and count tie.

Examples
- `recordScore("mia", 5), recordScore("ben", 4), recordScore("mia", 4), recordScore("ben", 5), recordScore("ben", 5), qualifiedAgents(2)` => `[ben, mia]`
- `recordScore("zoe", 4), recordScore("zoe", 4), recordScore("ava", 4), recordScore("kai", 5), qualifiedAgents(2)` => `[zoe]`
- `recordScore("bob", 5), recordScore("bob", 3), recordScore("ada", 4), recordScore("ada", 4), recordScore("cam", 4), qualifiedAgents(1)` => `[ada, bob, cam]`

examples.input: rate mia 5; rate ben 4; rate mia 4; rate ben 5; rate ben 5; query 2
rate zoe 4; rate zoe 4; rate ava 4; rate kai 5; query 2
rate bob 5; rate bob 3; rate ada 4; rate ada 4; rate cam 4; query 1

hints: Store only the running score sum and rating count for each agent instead of keeping every individual score.
Compare two averages `sumA / countA` and `sumB / countB` with 64-bit cross-multiplication (`sumA * countB` versus `sumB * countA`) to avoid truncation and floating-point rounding.

Filter agents meeting `minRatings` and sort them with a comparator chaining exact average, rating count, and `agentId`. Intended complexity for `n` agents: O(n log n) time for `qualifiedAgents` (`O(1)` average per `recordScore`) and O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: semicolon-separated operations rate <agent> <1..5> and query <minRatings>, for example: rate mia 5; rate ben 4; rate mia 4; rate ben 5; rate ben 5; query 2
sampleInput: rate mia 5; rate ben 4; rate mia 4; rate ben 5; rate ben 5; query 2
